subject: Environment gating: POC setup & next steps
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@medihealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@medihealth.com>, IT Security <itsec@medihealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Environment gating: POC setup & next steps

Irene — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The leadership team liked the performance numbers and we want to move the POC to the next step this month. Before we can spin up the evaluation environment, our security and infra teams need a short, explicit gating checklist so we can schedule work on our side.

High level asks from our side: 
- Org + API key provisioning: how are you mapping keys to environments and what permissions are needed?
- IP allowlist: we will only allow dedicated IPs into our staging VPC; need a list and guidance for ephemeral ranges.
- VPC peering: what are the subnets and route requirements; will Redwood require cross-account peering?
- Timeline: we need an expected activation window (ETA for keys + peering) so we can book the networking squad.

Can you send a simple mutual action plan (MAP) with owners and dates that I can attach to our ticket? If possible, include a one-page runbook for the on-call engineers (keys, certs, and common troubleshooting).

Thanks — Alice

--
Alice Park
Head of Platform Integrations
MediHealth
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment gating: POC setup & next steps

Alice — really glad to hear leadership is ready to proceed. Attached is a lightweight MAP template and a recommended sprint to complete environment activation. High-level summary below; I put owners against each line item so you can paste into your ticket.

MAP (summary) — target close: 2025-06-25
- API key & org setup (Owner: Irene Choi / Redwood) — deliverable: scoped API key pairs per team, 1 business day after kickoff.
- Firewall allowlist (Owner: MediHealth) — deliverable: CSV of public egress/ingress IPs; Redwood to confirm expected connection ports (we only need 443/TLS for API but peering may require additional ranges).
- VPC peering & routes (Owner: Karthik Iyer / Redwood + MediHealth NetOps) — deliverable: peering request + route table changes; target approval 3 business days.
- Test plan & smoke validation (Owner: Vanessa Ortiz / Redwood) — deliverable: runbook of three smoke checks (auth, basic inference, KV caching) within 24 hours of peering.

Quick notes on the specific asks you listed:
- API keys: we'll create sandbox-scoped keys that can be rotated. Keys are bound to an "org_id" and a set of allowed endpoints (we will send the exact permission JSON). We recommend issuing one key for your Staging team and one for CI. Keys are issued via the Console and we can pre-provision them if you want us to push them into your vault (Doc: redwood_onboarding_template.xlsx).
- IP allowlist: if you cannot do peering initially, we support static egress IPs from our Dedicated pool. If you prefer peering, we will need the MediHealth VPC CIDRs and a preferred subnet for the peering attachment.
- VPC peering: Redwood supports AWS VPC peering and Transit Gateway attachments. For the POC we recommend peering; we will provide exact cidr/route requirements once Karthik confirms which GPU cluster will host the reserved capacity.

I'm attaching the MAP template and a one-pager runbook. Karthik — can you add the peering CIDR and a rough ETA for cluster allocation? Vanessa — I'll work with you on the smoke tests; can we aim to validate within 24 hours of peering coming up?

Regards,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
(650) 555-0218

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2025 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Environment gating: POC setup & next steps

Adding the infra specifics from Redwood side.

Karthik notes:
- Cluster & IPs: We plan to allocate a staging cluster in us-west-2 (cluster-id: rw-stg-64). Public egress for the cluster comes from the Dedicated NAT pool: 52.23.192.0/27 (we will give 2 static addresses you can allow). If you prefer full private connectivity, Transit Gateway peering is supported — for the POC we can do a standard VPC peering attachment.
- Recommended peering CIDR whitelist: Redwood side: 10.8.0.0/16 (this is the cluster overlay; we will announce routes for the specific worker subnets after the peering is accepted). Please confirm your VPC CIDR(s) and a /24 or /22 preferred route range for the peering.
- IAM & roles: No cross-account IAM required for peering. For provisioning we will need a single service-account email to receive the pre-provisioned keys and the org_id.

Proposed short timeline (depends on MediHealth network lead availability):
- 2025-06-18: MediHealth provides VPC CIDR and allowlist CSV (Alice / NetOps).
- 2025-06-19: Redwood submits peering request and pre-provisions API keys (Irene / Karthik).
- 2025-06-20: NetOps accepts peering and confirms routes; smoke tests begin same day (Vanessa).
- 2025-06-23: POC validation complete and retrospective call.

If you want the Dedicated static egress IPs instead of peering initially, we can provide 2 IPs within 24 hours (that reduces operational lift on your side).

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
